702	// malformedSessionCRDTPath reports whether p targets the session-scoped CRDT
703	// namespace but is not at one of its four exact locations:
704	//
705	//	POST /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/ops
706	//	GET  /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/state
707	//	POST /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/compact
708	//	GET  /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/state/subscribe
709	//
710	// a missing "ops"/"state"/"compact"/"subscribe" segment, an extra segment, or
711	// a "crdt" segment in the keyword position (immediately past the document
712	// identifier) short of one of the registered shapes. ServeMux would answer
713	// those with a plain-text 404/405; every failure of these endpoints must be a
714	// JSON 400 instead. Empty segments are already rejected by the guard itself.
715	//
716	// "crdt" is treated as the endpoint keyword only in the fourth segment (index
717	// 3, right after the document identifier); a session or document identifier
718	// literally named "crdt" occupies an identifier position (index 0 or 2) and
719	// keeps its ordinary routes. Likewise "compact" is the endpoint keyword only
720	// in the fifth segment; a session or document literally named "compact" is an
721	// ordinary identifier.
722	func malformedSessionCRDTPath(p string) bool {
723		rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(p, "/v1/sessions/")
724		if !ok {
725			return false
726		}
727		segs := strings.Split(rest, "/")
728		if len(segs) < 4 || segs[1] != "documents" || segs[3] != "crdt" {
729			return false
730		}
731		// Keyword position reached. The batch commit, the state read and the
732		// compaction are all exactly
733		// {sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/{ops,state,compact}; the
734		// subscription adds one trailing "subscribe" segment.
735		validOps := len(segs) == 5 &&
736			segs[0] != "" &&
737			segs[2] != "" &&
738			segs[4] == "ops"
739		validState := len(segs) == 5 &&
740			segs[0] != "" &&
741			segs[2] != "" &&
742			segs[4] == "state"
743		validCompact := len(segs) == 5 &&
744			segs[0] != "" &&
745			segs[2] != "" &&
746			segs[4] == "compact"
747		validSubscribe := len(segs) == 6 &&
748			segs[0] != "" &&
749			segs[2] != "" &&
750			segs[4] == "state" &&
751			segs[5] == "subscribe"
752		return !(validOps || validState || validCompact || validSubscribe)
753	}

765	// decodeJSONBody enforces the strict POST contract shared by every JSON
766	// endpoint: Content-Type must be application/json, the body is capped at
767	// maxBatchBytes, it must contain exactly one JSON value, and no trailing data
768	// may follow it. Any violation writes a 400 JSON error and returns false; the
769	// caller returns immediately, so no handler reaches the store with malformed
770	// input and rejected requests write nothing.
771	func decodeJSONBody(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, dst any) bool {
772		mediaType, _, err := mime.ParseMediaType(r.Header.Get("Content-Type"))
773		if err != nil || mediaType != "application/json" {
774			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "Content-Type must be application/json")
775			return false
776		}

1195	// parseCursorPath reports whether raw is a decimal non-negative integer and
1196	// returns its value. Signs, fractions and other adornments are rejected.
1197	func parseCursorPath(raw string) (int64, bool) {
1198		if raw == "" {
1199			return 0, false
1200		}
1201		for _, c := range raw {
1202			if c < '0' || c > '9' {
1203				return 0, false
1204			}
1205		}
1206		n, err := strconv.ParseInt(raw, 10, 64)
1207		if err != nil {
1208			return 0, false
1209		}
1210		return n, true
1211	}

1213	// parseNonNegativeInt reports whether raw is a JSON integer >= 0. Floats,// strings, booleans, null and negative numbers are rejected.
1214	func parseNonNegativeInt(raw json.RawMessage) (int64, bool) {
1215		var n int64
1216		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &n); err != nil || n < 0 {
1217			return 0, false
1218		}
1219		// Guard against values like 1.0 that Unmarshal into int64 on some inputs;
1220		// require the literal to contain no fraction or exponent.
1221		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(string(raw))
1222		if trimmed == "" || trimmed[0] == '-' {
1223			return 0, false
1224		}
1225		for _, c := range trimmed {
1226			if c < '0' || c > '9' {
1227				return 0, false
1228			}
1229		}
1230		return n, true
1231	}

1234	// strings, booleans, null and negative numbers are rejected.
1235	func parsePositiveInt(raw json.RawMessage) (int64, bool) {
1236		n, ok := parseNonNegativeInt(raw)
1237		if !ok || n < 1 {
1238			return 0, false
1239		}
1240		return n, true
1241	}

1247		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &m); err != nil || m == nil {
1248			return false
1249		}
1250		return true

1335	// handleSessionPostChanges is the session-scoped batch commit over the same
1336	// change collection the session reads page:
1337	//
1338	//	POST /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/changes
1339	//
1340	// The request body carries only the changes array — the calling device is the
1341	// session's owning device, resolved with the same identity rule as the
1342	// session reads, exports and subscriptions; no new credential is introduced
1343	// and no device id travels in the body. Per-element semantics and the success
1344	// body are byte-identical to the document-level commit: results arrive in
1345	// request order, each naming its id, whether it was created and the cursor it
1346	// was assigned. The checks run in the fixed order request shape (400),
1347	// session existence (404), document permission (403) — the permission verdict
1348	// is taken inside the commit transaction, so a revoked device writes nothing —

14	// snapshotExportItem is one element of an export body. The struct field order
15	// fixes the on-the-wire key order to cursor then state; State is embedded as
16	// raw JSON so the stored content is emitted verbatim, exactly as the single
17	// snapshot read emits it.
18	type snapshotExportItem struct {
19		Cursor int64           `json:"cursor"`
20		State  json.RawMessage `json:"state"`
21	}
22	
23	// snapshotExportResponse is the export body with the top-level key order fixed
24	// to snapshots then count. Snapshots is always a non-nil slice so an empty
25	// export serializes as [] rather than null.
26	type snapshotExportResponse struct {
27		Snapshots []snapshotExportItem `json:"snapshots"`
28		Count     int                  `json:"count"`
29	}
30	
31	// handleExportSnapshots is the read-only batch export over a document's
32	// snapshot collection:
33	//
34	//	GET /v1/documents/{documentID}/snapshots?from=0&to=N
35	//
36	// from defaults to 0; to absent means no upper bound. Only snapshots whose
37	// cursor is in the closed [from, to] interval are returned, in ascending
38	// cursor order, at most one entry per cursor. An unknown document or a range
39	// without any snapshot is a successful 200 with an empty list and count 0, not
40	// an error. The handler writes nothing: it creates no snapshot, moves no
41	// cursor, records no change and notifies the push channels.
42	func handleExportSnapshots(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
43		documentID := r.PathValue("documentID") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
44	
45		from, to, ok := parseExportInterval(w, r.URL.Query())
46		if !ok {
47			return
48		}
49	
50		snaps, err := s.ExportSnapshots(documentID, from, to)
51		if err != nil {
52			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to export snapshots")
53			return
54		}
55		writeSnapshotExport(w, snaps)
56	}
57	
58	// writeSnapshotExport renders an export result in the shared response shape: a
59	// single compact JSON line with the snapshots,count key order, each item
60	// keyed cursor,state, an empty export serializing as [] with count 0. It is
61	// shared by the document-scoped and session-scoped exports so their bodies
62	// cannot drift apart.
63	func writeSnapshotExport(w http.ResponseWriter, snaps []events.ExportedSnapshot) {
64		items := make([]snapshotExportItem, 0, len(snaps))
65		for _, snap := range snaps {
66			items = append(items, snapshotExportItem{Cursor: snap.Cursor, State: snap.State})
67		}
68		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, snapshotExportResponse{Snapshots: items, Count: len(items)})
69	}
70	
71	// handleSessionExportSnapshots is the session-scoped view of the snapshot
72	// batch export, over the session document-read prefix with the resource
73	// segment swapped to the snapshot collection:
74	//
75	//	GET /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/snapshots?from=0&to=N
76	//
77	// The interval semantics and the response body are identical to the
78	// document-level export; the path offers no other read form, so every GET is
79	// the export (from/to absent means the default interval). Around the export
80	// sit the session view's checks in their fixed order — request shape and
81	// parameters (400), session existence (404), the session device's document
82	// permission (403) — so a rejected export exposes no snapshot content and
83	// writes nothing.
84	func handleSessionExportSnapshots(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
85		sessionID := r.PathValue("sessionId")   // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
86		documentID := r.PathValue("documentId") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
87	
88		// Malformed interval parameters are a request-shape error (400) checked
89		// before the resource lookup (404), matching the session change export's
90		// ordering.
91		from, to, ok := parseExportInterval(w, r.URL.Query())
92		if !ok {
93			return
94		}
95	
96		deviceID, err := s.SessionDevice(sessionID)
97		if err != nil {
98			if errors.Is(err, store.ErrSessionNotFound) {
99				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "session not found")
100				return
101			}
102			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to look up session")
103			return
104		}
105	
106		authorized, err := s.DocumentAuthorized(documentID, deviceID)
107		if err != nil {
108			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to look up permission")
109			return
110		}
111		if !authorized {
112			writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "device permission for this document has been revoked")
113			return
114		}
115	
116		snaps, err := s.ExportSnapshots(documentID, from, to)
117		if err != nil {
118			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to export snapshots")
119			return
120		}
121		writeSnapshotExport(w, snaps)
122	}
123	
124	// malformedSnapshotPath reports whether p targets the snapshot namespace but
125	// is not at one of its two exact locations:
126	//
127	//	GET  /v1/documents/{documentID}/snapshots          (the batch export)
128	//	GET  /v1/documents/{documentID}/snapshots/{cursor} (the single read)
129	//
130	// A trailing slash (an empty cursor segment, including the collection path
131	// with a trailing slash), extra path segments, or a "snapshots" segment in any
132	// keyword position short of one of those shapes is a malformed 400 rather than
133	// ServeMux's redirect or plain-text 404/405: the snapshot endpoints promise a
134	// JSON error and never a redirect. Empty segments are already rejected by the
135	// guard itself. The keyword is matched only past the documentID position, so a
136	// document literally named "snapshots" keeps its ordinary routes.
137	func malformedSnapshotPath(p string) bool {
138		rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(p, "/v1/documents/")
139		if !ok {
140			return false
141		}
142		segs := strings.Split(rest, "/")
143		for i, seg := range segs {
144			if seg != "snapshots" || i == 0 {
145				continue
146			}
147			// Keyword position reached. The collection is exactly
148			// {documentID}/snapshots; the single read adds one non-empty cursor
149			// segment. Anything else (trailing slash, missing/extra segments) is
150			// malformed.
151			collection := len(segs) == 2 && segs[0] != ""
152			item := len(segs) == 3 && segs[0] != "" && segs[2] != ""
153			return !(collection || item)
154		}
155		return false
156	}
157	
158	// malformedSessionSnapshotsPath reports whether p targets the session-scoped
159	// snapshot collection's shape but is not the collection's exact location
160	// (/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/snapshots): extra path
161	// segments past the collection (the session view has no single-snapshot
162	// item, so a trailing cursor segment is malformed too). ServeMux would answer
163	// those with a plain-text 404; the snapshot surface promises a JSON 400 and
164	// never a redirect. Empty segments (doubled slashes, a trailing slash) are
165	// already rejected by the guard itself.
166	//
167	// "snapshots" is treated as the collection keyword only in the fourth
168	// segment, right after the document identifier; a session or document
169	// identifier literally named "snapshots" occupies an identifier position and
170	// keeps its ordinary routes.
171	func malformedSessionSnapshotsPath(p string) bool {
172		rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(p, "/v1/sessions/")
173		if !ok {
174			return false
175		}
176		segs := strings.Split(rest, "/")
177		// The CRDT namespace ("crdt" immediately past the document identifier)
178		// has its own guard; "snapshots" there is an ordinary identifier, not
179		// this collection's keyword.
180		if len(segs) >= 4 && segs[1] == "documents" && segs[3] == "crdt" {
181			return false
182		}
183		if len(segs) < 4 || segs[1] != "documents" || segs[3] != "snapshots" {
184			return false
185		}
186		// Keyword position reached. The collection is exactly
187		// {sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/snapshots; anything past it is a
188		// malformed 400.
189		return !(len(segs) == 4 && segs[0] != "" && segs[2] != "")
190	}

14	// sessionRestoreRequest is the session-scoped restore body: only the change
15	// id and the snapshot cursor travel in the request. The calling device is the
16	// session's owning device resolved from the path, so a stray deviceId is
17	// decoded and ignored like every other unknown field.
18	type sessionRestoreRequest struct {
19		ChangeID       string          `json:"changeId"`
20		SnapshotCursor json.RawMessage `json:"snapshotCursor"`
21	}
22	
23	// handleSessionRestore is the session-scoped history restore, the session
24	// view's counterpart to POST /v1/documents/{documentID}/restore, mounted one
25	// segment below the session document resource:
26	//
27	//	POST /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/restore
28	//
29	// The body carries only changeId and snapshotCursor; the calling device is the
30	// session's owning device resolved from the path with the same identity rule
31	// as the session reads, exports, commits, replays, merges, polls and
32	// subscriptions — no new credential is introduced, and a stray deviceId in the
33	// body is ignored like any other unknown field. On a snapshot hit the snapshot
34	// state is appended as one ordinary change in a single serialized transaction:
35	// old rows are untouched and the document cursor advances by one. The success
36	// body is byte-identical to the document-level restore: id, created, the
37	// assigned cursor and the source snapshot cursor. The checks run in the fixed
38	// order request shape (400), session existence (404), document permission
39	// (403) — the permission verdict is taken inside the restore transaction, so a
40	// revoked device writes nothing — followed by the snapshot lookup (a miss, an
41	// unknown document included, is 404) and the idempotency/conflict verdict (an
42	// id occupied by an ordinary change, or a restore whose device, snapshot
43	// cursor or source state differs, is 409). Every rejection leaves the log
44	// untouched.
45	func handleSessionRestore(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
46		sessionID := r.PathValue("sessionId")   // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
47		documentID := r.PathValue("documentId") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
48	
49		var req sessionRestoreRequest
50		if !decodeJSONBody(w, r, &req) {
51			return
52		}
53		if req.ChangeID == "" {
54			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "changeId must be a non-empty string")
55			return
56		}
57		// snapshotCursor must be present and a positive integer (no fractions,
58		// strings, booleans, null or zero).
59		if len(req.SnapshotCursor) == 0 {
60			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "snapshotCursor must be a positive integer")
61			return
62		}
63		snapshotCursor, ok := parsePositiveInt(req.SnapshotCursor)
64		if !ok {
65			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "snapshotCursor must be a positive integer")
66			return
67		}
68	
69		// Request shape is settled; only now does the session lookup run, so a
70		// malformed restore against an unknown session is still a 400.
71		deviceID, err := s.SessionDevice(sessionID)
72		if err != nil {
73			if errors.Is(err, store.ErrSessionNotFound) {
74				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "session not found")
75				return
76			}
77			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to look up session")
78			return
79		}
80	
81		result, err := s.RestoreSessionSnapshot(documentID, deviceID, req.ChangeID, snapshotCursor)
82		if err != nil {
83			var conflict *events.ErrRestoreConflict
84			switch {
85			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrDeviceNotFound):
86				// The session's device was deregistered between the lookup and the
87				// restore; its cascade removed the session too, so the identity the
88				// caller used no longer exists.
89				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "session not found")
90			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrPermissionDenied):
91				writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "device permission for this document has been revoked")
92			case errors.Is(err, events.ErrSnapshotNotFound):
93				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "snapshot not found")
94			case errors.As(err, &conflict):
95				writeError(w, http.StatusConflict, "change id already exists with a different deviceId, snapshotCursor or source state: "+req.ChangeID)
96			default:
97				writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to restore snapshot")
98			}
99			return
100		}
101	
102		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, result)
103	}
104	
105	// malformedSessionRestorePath reports whether p targets the session-scoped
106	// restore endpoint but is not at its exact location
107	// (/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/restore): a missing
108	// "documents" segment, an extra segment, or a "restore" segment in a position
109	// short of the registered shape. ServeMux would answer those with a
110	// plain-text 404 (or a redirect for an empty segment); every failure of this
111	// endpoint must be a JSON 400 instead. Empty segments are already rejected by
112	// the guard itself.
113	//
114	// "restore" is treated as the endpoint keyword only in its terminal segment
115	// position (the fourth segment, index 3); a session or document identifier
116	// literally named "restore" occupies an identifier position (index 0 or 2) and
117	// is therefore left to the ordinary session routes like any other id.
118	func malformedSessionRestorePath(p string) bool {
119		rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(p, "/v1/sessions/")
120		if !ok {
121			return false
122		}
123		segs := strings.Split(rest, "/")
124		// The CRDT namespace ("crdt" immediately past the document identifier)
125		// has its own guard; "restore" there is an ordinary identifier, not the
126		// restore keyword.
127		if len(segs) >= 4 && segs[1] == "documents" && segs[3] == "crdt" {
128			return false
129		}
130		for i, seg := range segs {
131			if seg != "restore" {
132				continue
133			}
134			// Identifier positions: sessionId (0) and documentId (2). A value of
135			// "restore" there is an ordinary identifier, not the endpoint word.
136			if i == 0 || i == 2 {
137				continue
138			}
139			// Endpoint keyword position: the fourth segment must be exactly
140			// "restore" with the documents scaffolding around it, and no segment
141			// may follow. Any other occurrence is a malformed path.
142			if i == 3 && len(segs) == 4 &&
143				segs[0] != "" &&
144				segs[1] == "documents" &&
145				segs[2] != "" {
146				return false
147			}
148			return true
149		}
150		return false
151	}

1	// Package app is the composition root: it opens the one shared database and
2	// constructs the three independently reusable internal services — the change
3	// event service, the permission service and the CRDT state service — wiring
4	// them together only through their internal interfaces.
5	//
6	// The services share one SQLite connection (the kernel opens a single
7	// pooled connection with immediate transactions), so a change commit, a CRDT
8	// submission or compaction, and a permission change are serialized on the
9	// same connection and leave no half-written batch. The change event and CRDT
10	// services take their registration-and-authorization verdict from the
11	// permission service inside their own transactions (events.Gate / crdt.Gate),
12	// and the permission service fans a committed revoke out to their
13	// subscription registries through authz.RevokeSink. No service reaches into
14	// another service's tables or fields.
15	//
16	// App is the single object the entry and HTTP layers use. It promotes each
17	// service's input/output boundary as its methods while hiding the wiring; it
18	// adds no authentication and exposes no endpoint of its own.
19	package app
20	
21	import (
22		"context"
23		"encoding/json"
24		"time"
25	
26		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/authz"
27		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/crdt"
28		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/events"
29		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/push"
30		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/store"
31	)
32	
33	// App composes the durable kernel and the three internal services over one
34	// shared database connection.
35	type App struct {
36		*store.Store
37	
38		events *events.Service
39		crdt   *crdt.Service
40	
41		// pushSubs is the process-wide, in-memory registry of the live push
42		// connections across both channels. It backs the device-scoped
43		// subscription management endpoints and holds no durable state.
44		pushSubs *push.Registry
45	
46		// Authz is the permission service. It is exposed so the HTTP layer can
47		// grant/revoke and read authorization directly; the other services reach
48		// it through their gates rather than this field.
49		Authz *authz.Service
50	}
51	
52	// Open opens (creating if needed) the SQLite database at path and constructs
53	// every internal service over it. The empty path opens a private in-memory
54	// database useful for tests. A construction failure closes the kernel and
55	// leaves nothing behind.
56	func Open(path string) (*App, error) {
57		kernel, err := store.Open(path)
58		if err != nil {
59			return nil, err
60		}
61	
62		// The permission service is built first: its gate is a constructor
63		// dependency of the change event and CRDT services.
64		permissions, err := authz.New(kernel)
65		if err != nil {
66			_ = kernel.Close()
67			return nil, err
68		}
69		eventService, err := events.New(kernel, permissions)
70		if err != nil {
71			_ = kernel.Close()
72			return nil, err
73		}
74		crdtService, err := crdt.New(kernel, permissions)
75		if err != nil {
76			_ = kernel.Close()
77			return nil, err
78		}
79	
80		// A committed revoke ends the affected live subscriptions in both
81		// push channels. The dependency is an interface, registered once here, so
82		// the permission service never names either subscriber concretely.
83		permissions.AddRevokeSink(eventsRevokeSink{eventService})
84		permissions.AddRevokeSink(crdtService)
85	
86		return &App{
87			Store:    kernel,
88			events:   eventService,
89			crdt:     crdtService,
90			Authz:    permissions,
91			pushSubs: push.NewRegistry(),
92		}, nil
93	}
94	
95	// eventsRevokeSink adapts the change event service's revoke hook to the
96	// permission service's RevokeSink interface.
97	type eventsRevokeSink struct{ e *events.Service }
98	
99	func (s eventsRevokeSink) PermissionRevoked(documentID, deviceID string) {
100		s.e.SignalRevoked(documentID, deviceID)
101	}
102	
103	// Events returns the change event service.
104	func (a *App) Events() *events.Service { return a.events }
105	
106	// CRDT returns the CRDT state service.
107	func (a *App) CRDT() *crdt.Service { return a.crdt }
108	
109	// ---- Change event service boundary (promoted so the entry layer has one
110	// object; each method delegates verbatim to the events service). ----
111	
112	// InterruptWaits wakes every parked long poll and every live change-log and
113	// CRDT subscription without closing the database, so an orderly shutdown
114	// drains waiting connections (long polls answer 503; subscriptions finish
115	// with the going-away close) instead of holding the drain hostage.
116	func (a *App) InterruptWaits() {
117		a.events.InterruptWaits()
118		a.crdt.InterruptWaits()
119	}
120	
121	// Closing reports whether shutdown has begun, covering both push channels.
122	func (a *App) Closing() bool {
123		return a.events.Closing() || a.crdt.Closing()
124	}
125	
126	// Close interrupts the in-memory observers, waits for every subscription
127	// handler to unregister and then releases the shared database handle.
128	func (a *App) Close() error {
129		a.events.InterruptWaits()
130		a.crdt.InterruptWaits()
131		a.events.WaitDrained()
132		a.crdt.WaitDrained()
133		return a.Store.Close()
134	}
135	
136	// PostChanges delegates to the change event service.
137	func (a *App) PostChanges(documentID string, changes []events.Change) ([]events.Result, error) {
138		return a.events.PostChanges(documentID, changes)
139	}
140	
141	// ReplayChanges delegates to the change event service.
142	func (a *App) ReplayChanges(documentID string, changes []events.Change) ([]events.Result, error) {
143		return a.events.ReplayChanges(documentID, changes)
144	}
145	
146	// PostSessionChanges commits a batch whose device identity was resolved from
147	// a session by the HTTP layer, delegating to the change event service's
148	// gated commit: the registration/permission verdict is taken inside the same
149	// serialized transaction as the write, so a revoked device commits nothing.
150	func (a *App) PostSessionChanges(documentID string, changes []events.Change) ([]events.Result, error) {
151		return a.events.CommitAuthorized(documentID, changes)
152	}
153	
154	// ReplaySessionChanges replays an offline batch whose device identity was
155	// resolved from a session by the HTTP layer; it is the session counterpart
156	// to ReplayChanges and commits through the same gated transaction the
157	// session-scoped batch commit uses, so the two paths cannot drift.
158	func (a *App) ReplaySessionChanges(documentID string, changes []events.Change) ([]events.Result, error) {
159		return a.events.CommitAuthorized(documentID, changes)
160	}
161	
162	// MergeChange delegates to the change event service.
163	func (a *App) MergeChange(documentID string, baseCursor int64, c events.Change) (events.MergeResult, error) {
164		return a.events.MergeChange(documentID, baseCursor, c)
165	}
166	
167	// MergeSessionChange merges a single change whose device identity was resolved
168	// from a session by the HTTP layer, delegating to the change event service's
169	// gated merge: the registration/permission verdict is taken inside the same
170	// serialized transaction as the merge judgment and append, so a revoked device
171	// writes nothing and a rejected request observes no change content.
172	func (a *App) MergeSessionChange(documentID string, baseCursor int64, c events.Change) (events.MergeResult, error) {
173		return a.events.MergeChangeAuthorized(documentID, baseCursor, c)
174	}
175	
176	// PutSnapshot delegates to the change event service.
177	func (a *App) PutSnapshot(documentID string, cursor int64, state json.RawMessage) (bool, error) {
178		return a.events.PutSnapshot(documentID, cursor, state)
179	}
180	
181	// GetSnapshot delegates to the change event service.
182	func (a *App) GetSnapshot(documentID string, cursor int64) (json.RawMessage, error) {
183		return a.events.GetSnapshot(documentID, cursor)

249	// DeregisterDevice removes a registered device together with every record it
250	// owns — its sessions, the attachments it created (chunks, sealed state and
251	// unfinished uploads included), the access grants it held, and its
252	// document-permission rows — all in one serialized transaction that commits
253	// synchronously. An unknown or already deregistered device yields
254	// store.ErrDeviceNotFound and writes nothing, so a repeat deregistration
255	// misses exactly the way a never-registered id does and concurrent calls take
256	// effect at most once. Shared digest-addressed content is reclaimed only when
257	// the last completed attachment referencing it is gone; other devices'
258	// changes, snapshots and document content are untouched.
259	//
260	// After the commit the same id may register again as a brand-new device — no
261	// session, permission or attachment is inherited — and every live
262	// subscription the device held across both push channels is ended
263	// immediately, stickily.
264	func (a *App) DeregisterDevice(deviceID string) error {
265		tx, err := a.Store.DB().Begin()
266		if err != nil {
267			return err
268		}
269		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
270	
271		if err := store.DeleteDeviceTx(tx, deviceID); err != nil {
272			return err
273		}
274		if err := a.Authz.DeleteDevicePermissionsTx(tx, deviceID); err != nil {
275			return err
276		}
277		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
278			return err
279		}
280	
281		// End the device's live subscriptions only after the cascade is durable:
282		// a reconnect attempt after the close finds the backing session gone
283		// (404), so the connection cannot immediately re-establish itself.
284		a.events.SignalDeviceDeregistered(deviceID)
285		a.crdt.SignalDeviceDeregistered(deviceID)
286		return nil
287	}

289	// ---- Document-level deletion. ----
290	
291	// DeleteDocument removes a registered device's whole document in one
292	// serialized, synchronously committed transaction. The calling device is
293	// declared by deviceId — no new authentication is introduced.
294	//
295	// The fixed verdict order is taken inside the transaction, before any cleanup:
296	//
297	//   - an unregistered device yields store.ErrDeviceNotFound (404) and writes
298	//     nothing;
299	//   - a device whose permission for the document was revoked yields
300	//     store.ErrPermissionDenied (403) and no cleanup runs;
301	//   - a document with no durable data anywhere — never created or already
302	//     deleted — yields events.ErrDocumentNotFound (404) and writes nothing.
303	//
304	// On success every row of the document is removed as one judgment: its online
305	// and trimmed change log, the retained idempotency summaries, its snapshots,
306	// its CRDT state and the per-document permission ledger. The same id is a
307	// brand-new document afterward — the cursor space restarts at 1 — and
308	// inherits no history. Concurrent deletes commit at most once because the
309	// existence verdict and the deletions share one immediate transaction on the
310	// single connection.
311	//
312	// Only after the commit is durable are the document's live subscriptions
313	// ended (close code 4420 on both push channels) and dropped from the
314	// management registry; other documents' and devices' connections are
315	// untouched.
316	func (a *App) DeleteDocument(documentID, deviceID string) error {
317		tx, err := a.Store.DB().Begin()
318		if err != nil {
319			return err
320		}
321		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
322	
323		// Registration first, then permission, both before any document content
324		// is observed: a rejected delete reveals nothing and cleans nothing.
325		if err := a.Authz.AuthorizedTx(tx, documentID, deviceID); err != nil {
326			return err
327		}
328	
329		eventsExist, err := a.events.DocumentDataExistsTx(tx, documentID)
330		if err != nil {
331			return err
332		}
333		crdtExist, err := a.crdt.DocumentDataExistsTx(tx, documentID)
334		if err != nil {
335			return err
336		}
337		// A ledger-only deviation row also counts as document data, so a document
338		// whose only durable trace is a grant/revoke still deletes cleanly and the
339		// re-created id inherits no authorization state.
340		ledgerExist, err := a.Authz.DocumentHasRowsTx(tx, documentID)
341		if err != nil {
342			return err
343		}
344		if !eventsExist && !crdtExist && !ledgerExist {
345			return events.ErrDocumentNotFound
346		}
347	
348		if err := a.events.DeleteDocumentDataTx(tx, documentID); err != nil {
349			return err
350		}
351		if err := a.crdt.DeleteDocumentDataTx(tx, documentID); err != nil {
352			return err
353		}
354		if err := a.Authz.DeleteDocumentPermissionsTx(tx, documentID); err != nil {
355			return err
356		}
357	
358		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
359			return err
360		}
361	
362		// End the document's live subscriptions on both channels and drop them
363		// from the management registry only after the cleanup is durable: the
364		// close is one-shot per connection, so a client re-subscribing to the
365		// now-fresh id opens a new connection and never reopens the ended ones.
366		a.events.SignalDocumentDeleted(documentID)
367		a.crdt.SignalDocumentDeleted(documentID)
368		a.CloseDocumentPush(documentID)
369		return nil
370	}

1	// Package events is the change event service: the durable per-document change
2	// log together with everything written on top of it.
3	//
4	// Within a document every change has a client-supplied id. New ids receive a
5	// monotonically increasing cursor; re-posting an existing id is idempotent
6	// only when the deviceId and decoded JSON payload match, otherwise it is a
7	// conflict. Valid batches commit atomically in one serialized transaction, so
8	// cursors never repeat and no record is partially written, even under
9	// concurrent writers. Ordinary posts, offline replays, merges and snapshot
10	// restores all allocate from the same per-document contiguous cursor space.
11	//
12	// A document may also carry snapshots: caller-supplied JSON states pinned to
13	// existing change cursors. Snapshots are write-once per cursor — a matching
14	// re-post is idempotent, a differing one a conflict — and live apart from the
15	// change log. A restore appends an ordinary change whose payload is a
16	// snapshot's state, recording its provenance so a repeated restore after a
17	// restart keeps the same idempotency/conflict decisions.
18	//
19	// Reads page by cursor in ascending order. The session view and the document
20	// view are the same read; the HTTP layer adds the session/permission checks.
21	// Long polling and push subscriptions are in-memory observers of commits:
22	// they register before the confirming read, hold no durable state, and are
23	// woken only after a change-bearing transaction has committed.
24	//
25	// The service owns only its own tables. The registration and permission
26	// layers are reached through its Gate interface, so a replay or merge never
27	// reaches into another service's storage.
28	package events
29	
30	import (
31		"encoding/json"
32		"errors"
33		"fmt"
34	)
35	
36	// ErrStoreClosing reports that the service is shutting down and parked long
37	// polls have been woken so they can return without writing anything. The
38	// caller maps it to 503.
39	var ErrStoreClosing = errors.New("store is closing")
40	
41	// Change is one element of an inbound batch or one row of a listing.
42	type Change struct {
43		ID       string          // client-supplied change id, unique per document
44		DeviceID string          // originating device
45		Payload  json.RawMessage // decoded JSON value, stored verbatim
46	}
47	
48	// Result reports the outcome for one element of an accepted batch.
49	type Result struct {
50		ID      string `json:"id"`
51		Created bool   `json:"created"`
52		Cursor  int64  `json:"cursor"`
53	}
54	
55	// ListedChange is one row in a ListChanges response.
56	type ListedChange struct {
57		ID       string          `json:"id"`
58		DeviceID string          `json:"deviceId"`
59		Payload  json.RawMessage `json:"payload"`
60		Cursor   int64           `json:"cursor"`
61	}
62	
63	// MergeResult reports the outcome of an accepted MergeChange. Outcome is one
64	// of "idempotent", "applied" or "merged".
65	type MergeResult struct {
66		ID      string  `json:"id"`
67		Outcome string  `json:"outcome"`
68		Cursor  int64   `json:"cursor"`
69		Result  *Result `json:"result,omitempty"`
70	}
71	
72	// ErrConflict reports that a batch references an existing change id with a
73	// different deviceId or payload. The whole batch is rejected.
74	type ErrConflict struct {
75		ID string
76	}
77	
78	func (e *ErrConflict) Error() string {
79		return fmt.Sprintf("conflicting change %q for document", e.ID)
80	}
81	
82	// ErrStaleCursor reports that a merge targets a base cursor for an unknown
83	// document, or a base cursor greater than the document's current cursor. The
84	// caller maps it to 400; nothing is written.
85	var ErrStaleCursor = errors.New("baseCursor is unknown or ahead of the current cursor")
86	
87	// ErrSnapshotBase reports that a snapshot targets an unknown document or a
88	// cursor that is not an existing change cursor of the document. The caller
89	// maps it to 400; nothing is written.
90	var ErrSnapshotBase = errors.New("snapshot cursor is not an existing cursor of the document")
91	
92	// ErrCompactedBase reports that a merge targets a base cursor below the
93	// document's compaction boundary: the changes it would be checked against
94	// have left the online log, so the conflict check cannot be completed. The
95	// caller maps it to 400; nothing is written.
96	var ErrCompactedBase = errors.New("baseCursor is below the compaction boundary")
97	
98	// ErrSnapshotNotFound reports that no snapshot exists for the document and
99	// cursor. The caller maps it to 404.
100	var ErrSnapshotNotFound = errors.New("snapshot not found")
101	
102	// ErrSnapshotConflict reports that a snapshot already exists for the document
103	// and cursor with a different state. The stored snapshot is left unchanged.
104	type ErrSnapshotConflict struct {
105		Cursor int64
106	}
107	
108	func (e *ErrSnapshotConflict) Error() string {
109		return fmt.Sprintf("conflicting snapshot for cursor %d", e.Cursor)
110	}
111	
112	// ErrRestoreConflict reports that a restore references a change id that is
113	// already taken by an ordinary change, or by a prior restore whose deviceId,
114	// snapshot cursor or source state differs. Nothing is written; the caller maps
115	// it to 409.
116	type ErrRestoreConflict struct {
117		ID string
118	}
119	
120	func (e *ErrRestoreConflict) Error() string {
121		return fmt.Sprintf("change id %q conflicts with the change log", e.ID)
122	}
123	
124	// ExportedSnapshot is one row of an ExportSnapshots result.
125	type ExportedSnapshot struct {
126		Cursor int64           `json:"cursor"`
127		State  json.RawMessage `json:"state"`
128	}
129	
130	// RestoreResult reports the outcome of an accepted RestoreSnapshot.
131	type RestoreResult struct {
132		ID           string `json:"id"`
133		Created      bool   `json:"created"`
134		Cursor       int64  `json:"cursor"`
135		RestoredFrom int64  `json:"restoredFrom"`
136	}
137	
138	// schema is created when the service is constructed. Table and index shapes
139	// are unchanged from the pre-refactor layout, so data already on disk stays
140	// readable.
141	const schema = `
142	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS changes (
143		document_id TEXT NOT NULL,
144		cursor      INTEGER NOT NULL,
145		id          TEXT NOT NULL,
146		device_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
147		payload     BLOB NOT NULL,
148		PRIMARY KEY (document_id, id)
149	);
150	CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS changes_doc_cursor_idx
151		ON changes(document_id, cursor);
152	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS snapshots (
153		document_id TEXT NOT NULL,
154		cursor      INTEGER NOT NULL,
155		state       BLOB NOT NULL,
156		PRIMARY KEY (document_id, cursor)
157	);
158	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS restores (
159		document_id     TEXT NOT NULL,
160		change_id       TEXT NOT NULL,
161		device_id       TEXT NOT NULL,
162		snapshot_cursor INTEGER NOT NULL,
163		change_cursor   INTEGER NOT NULL,
164		state           BLOB NOT NULL,
165		PRIMARY KEY (document_id, change_id)
166	);
167	CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS restores_doc_cursor_idx
168		ON restores(document_id, change_cursor);
169	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS change_boundaries (
170		document_id TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
171		boundary    INTEGER NOT NULL
172	);
173	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS change_identities (
174		document_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
175		id            TEXT NOT NULL,
176		device_id     TEXT NOT NULL,
177		digest        BLOB NOT NULL,
178		cursor        INTEGER NOT NULL,
179		restored_from INTEGER,
180		PRIMARY KEY (document_id, id)
181	);
182	`

1	package events
2	
3	import (
4		"bytes"
5		"database/sql"
6		"encoding/json"
7		"errors"
8	
9		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/store"
10	)
11	
12	// PutSnapshot stores state as the snapshot of documentID at cursor, creating
13	// it on first use and reporting whether this call created it.
14	//
15	// Only cursors of existing changes are valid snapshot points: an unknown
16	// document, a cursor below 1 or a cursor ahead of the document's current
17	// cursor yields ErrSnapshotBase and nothing is written. The current cursor is
18	// the document's high-water mark in the never-reset cursor space — the
19	// greater of the online maximum and the compaction boundary — so a cursor
20	// whose change has been trimmed by compaction is still a valid snapshot
21	// point, even after a full trim emptied the online log. Re-posting a state
22	// that decodes equal to the stored one is idempotent (created=false); a
23	// different state is an *ErrSnapshotConflict and the stored snapshot is left
24	// unchanged. Snapshots are independent of the change log: they neither move
25	// the document's cursor nor affect merges.
26	func (s *Service) PutSnapshot(documentID string, cursor int64, state json.RawMessage) (bool, error) {
27		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
28		if err != nil {
29			return false, err
30		}
31		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
32	
33		current, err := currentCursorTx(tx, documentID)
34		if err != nil {
35			return false, err
36		}
37		if current == 0 || cursor < 1 || cursor > current {
38			return false, ErrSnapshotBase
39		}
40	
41		var existing []byte
42		err = tx.QueryRow(
43			`SELECT state FROM snapshots WHERE document_id = ? AND cursor = ?`,
44			documentID, cursor,
45		).Scan(&existing)
46		switch {
47		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
48			if _, err := tx.Exec(
49				`INSERT INTO snapshots (document_id, cursor, state) VALUES (?, ?, ?)`,
50				documentID, cursor, []byte(state),
51			); err != nil {
52				return false, err
53			}
54			if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
55				return false, err
56			}
57			return true, nil
58		case err != nil:
59			return false, err
60		default:
61			if !store.JSONEqual(existing, state) {
62				return false, &ErrSnapshotConflict{Cursor: cursor}
63			}
64			return false, nil
65		}
66	}
67	
68	// GetSnapshot returns the state stored for documentID at cursor. Any miss —
69	// unknown document, unknown cursor or absent snapshot — yields
70	// ErrSnapshotNotFound.
71	func (s *Service) GetSnapshot(documentID string, cursor int64) (json.RawMessage, error) {
72		var state []byte
73		err := s.db.QueryRow(
74			`SELECT state FROM snapshots WHERE document_id = ? AND cursor = ?`,
75			documentID, cursor,
76		).Scan(&state)
77		switch {
78		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
79			return nil, ErrSnapshotNotFound
80		case err != nil:
81			return nil, err
82		default:
83			return json.RawMessage(state), nil
84		}
85	}
86	
87	// ExportSnapshots returns every snapshot of documentID whose cursor lies in
88	// the closed interval [from, to], in ascending cursor order. When to is nil no
89	// upper bound is applied. An unknown document, or a range without a snapshot,
90	// yields an empty list and no error: the export is a read that misses like any
91	// other. The (document_id, cursor) primary key guarantees a cursor appears at
92	// most once.
93	//
94	// The single SELECT runs as one SQLite statement over the serialized
95	// connection, so a snapshot committed concurrently is observed either with all
96	// of its row or not at all — never half of it. The read starts no
97	// transaction, writes nothing and notifies no waiters, so it cannot move a
98	// cursor or produce a change record.
99	func (s *Service) ExportSnapshots(documentID string, from int64, to *int64) ([]ExportedSnapshot, error) {
100		var (
101			rows *sql.Rows
102			err  error
103		)
104		if to == nil {
105			rows, err = s.db.Query(
106				`SELECT cursor, state FROM snapshots
107				 WHERE document_id = ? AND cursor >= ?
108				 ORDER BY cursor ASC`,
109				documentID, from,
110			)
111		} else {
112			rows, err = s.db.Query(
113				`SELECT cursor, state FROM snapshots
114				 WHERE document_id = ? AND cursor >= ? AND cursor <= ?
115				 ORDER BY cursor ASC`,
116				documentID, from, *to,
117			)
118		}
119		if err != nil {
120			return nil, err
121		}
122		defer func() { _ = rows.Close() }()
123	
124		out := make([]ExportedSnapshot, 0)
125		for rows.Next() {
126			var snap ExportedSnapshot
127			if err := rows.Scan(&snap.Cursor, &snap.State); err != nil {
128				return nil, err
129			}
130			out = append(out, snap)
131		}
132		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
133			return nil, err
134		}
135		return out, nil
136	}
137	
138	// RestoreSnapshot appends one ordinary change whose payload is the state of
139	// documentID's snapshot at snapshotCursor, all within a single serialized
140	// transaction.
141	//
142	//   - A snapshot miss (unknown document or a cursor without a snapshot)
143	//     returns ErrSnapshotNotFound; nothing is written.
144	//   - If changeID already belongs to a prior restore, the call is idempotent
145	//     only when deviceId, snapshotCursor and the decoded source state all
146	//     match; the first result (created=false, original cursor) is returned.
147	//   - If changeID is taken by an ordinary change, or a restore whose provenance
148	//     differs, the call returns *ErrRestoreConflict; nothing is written.
149	//
150	// Otherwise a new change is appended with the next document cursor and the
151	// restore provenance is recorded. Old rows are never modified.
152	func (s *Service) RestoreSnapshot(documentID, deviceID, changeID string, snapshotCursor int64) (RestoreResult, error) {
153		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
154		if err != nil {
155			return RestoreResult{}, err
156		}
157		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
158	
159		result, err := restoreSnapshotTx(tx, documentID, deviceID, changeID, snapshotCursor)
160		if err != nil {
161			return RestoreResult{}, err
162		}
163		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
164			return RestoreResult{}, err
165		}
166		// A genuinely new restore appended a change and is the only outcome that
167		// wakes the long polls and pushes to subscribers; an idempotent repeat
168		// appended nothing and notifies nothing.
169		if result.Created {
170			s.notifyWaiters(documentID)
171		}
172		return result, nil
173	}
174	
175	// RestoreSnapshotAuthorized is the session-scoped restore: it has exactly the
176	// restore semantics of RestoreSnapshot, but enforces the gate (registration
177	// then permission) first in the same serialized transaction: an unregistered
178	// device yields store.ErrDeviceNotFound and a revoked device yields
179	// ErrPermissionDenied. None of those outcomes writes anything or observes
180	// snapshot or change content. The device identity is resolved from the session
181	// by the HTTP layer before the call.
182	func (s *Service) RestoreSnapshotAuthorized(documentID, deviceID, changeID string, snapshotCursor int64) (RestoreResult, error) {
183		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
184		if err != nil {
185			return RestoreResult{}, err
186		}
187		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
188	
189		// Gate first: the device row and the permission row are read before the
190		// snapshot is looked up or any change content is observed, so a rejected
191		// restore cannot reveal anything.
192		if s.gate != nil {
193			if err := s.gate.DeviceAuthorizedTx(tx, documentID, deviceID); err != nil {
194				return RestoreResult{}, err
195			}
196		}
197	
198		result, err := restoreSnapshotTx(tx, documentID, deviceID, changeID, snapshotCursor)
199		if err != nil {
200			return RestoreResult{}, err
201		}
202		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
203			return RestoreResult{}, err
204		}
205		if result.Created {
206			s.notifyWaiters(documentID)
207		}
208		return result, nil
209	}
210	
211	// restoreSnapshotTx runs the snapshot lookup, the idempotency/conflict
212	// resolution and the single append inside the caller's serialized
213	// transaction. It is shared by the document-level restore and the
214	// session-scoped authorized restore so the two paths cannot drift: both take
215	// their snapshot miss (ErrSnapshotNotFound), conflict (*ErrRestoreConflict)
216	// and append decisions from one code path. The result's Created flag tells
217	// the caller whether a change-bearing transaction just committed and the push
218	// channels therefore need waking.
219	func restoreSnapshotTx(tx *sql.Tx, documentID, deviceID, changeID string, snapshotCursor int64) (RestoreResult, error) {
220		// The snapshot must exist; its state is the payload to append.
221		var state []byte
222		err := tx.QueryRow(
223			`SELECT state FROM snapshots WHERE document_id = ? AND cursor = ?`,
224			documentID, snapshotCursor,
225		).Scan(&state)
226		switch {
227		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
228			return RestoreResult{}, ErrSnapshotNotFound
229		case err != nil:
230			return RestoreResult{}, err
231		}
232	
233		// Resolve the change id: an ordinary row, a prior restore and a
234		// compacted-away id's retained summary are handled differently, so consult
235		// all three.
236		var existingCursor int64
237		var existingDevice string
238		var existingPayload []byte
239		err = tx.QueryRow(
240			`SELECT cursor, device_id, payload FROM changes WHERE document_id = ? AND id = ?`,
241			documentID, changeID,
242		).Scan(&existingCursor, &existingDevice, &existingPayload)
243		switch {
244		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
245			// No online row: the id may belong to a change compaction trimmed.
246			// Its retained summary still decides — an idempotent restore needs the
247			// same device, snapshot cursor and source state; an id left by an
248			// ordinary trimmed change is a conflict, as is any mismatch.
249			var summaryDevice string
250			var summaryDigest []byte
251			var summaryCursor int64
252			var restoredFrom sql.NullInt64
253			err := tx.QueryRow(
254				`SELECT device_id, digest, cursor, restored_from FROM change_identities
255				 WHERE document_id = ? AND id = ?`,
256				documentID, changeID,
257			).Scan(&summaryDevice, &summaryDigest, &summaryCursor, &restoredFrom)
258			switch {
259			case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
260				// Genuinely new id; fall through to append below.
261			case err != nil:
262				return RestoreResult{}, err
263			default:
264				stateDigest, err := payloadDigest(state)
265				if err != nil {
266					return RestoreResult{}, err
267				}
268				if !restoredFrom.Valid || restoredFrom.Int64 != snapshotCursor ||
269					summaryDevice != deviceID || !bytes.Equal(summaryDigest, stateDigest) {
270					return RestoreResult{}, &ErrRestoreConflict{ID: changeID}
271				}
272				return RestoreResult{
273					ID:           changeID,
274					Created:      false,
275					Cursor:       summaryCursor,
276					RestoredFrom: snapshotCursor,
277				}, nil
278			}
279		case err != nil:
280			return RestoreResult{}, err
281		default:
282			var restDevice string
283			var restSnapshotCursor int64
284			var restState []byte
285			err = tx.QueryRow(
286				`SELECT device_id, snapshot_cursor, state FROM restores WHERE document_id = ? AND change_id = ?`,
287				documentID, changeID,
288			).Scan(&restDevice, &restSnapshotCursor, &restState)
289			switch {
290			case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
291				// The id belongs to an ordinary change (or a batch/merge change),
292				// not a restore: never treat it as an idempotent restore.
293				return RestoreResult{}, &ErrRestoreConflict{ID: changeID}
294			case err != nil:
295				return RestoreResult{}, err
296			default:
297				if restDevice != deviceID || restSnapshotCursor != snapshotCursor || !store.JSONEqual(restState, state) {
298					return RestoreResult{}, &ErrRestoreConflict{ID: changeID}
299				}
300				return RestoreResult{
301					ID:           changeID,
302					Created:      false,
303					Cursor:       existingCursor,
304					RestoredFrom: snapshotCursor,
305				}, nil
306			}
307		}
308	
309		nextCursor, err := currentCursorTx(tx, documentID)
310		if err != nil {
311			return RestoreResult{}, err
312		}
313		nextCursor++
314		if _, err := tx.Exec(
315			`INSERT INTO changes (document_id, cursor, id, device_id, payload) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)`,
316			documentID, nextCursor, changeID, deviceID, state,
317		); err != nil {
318			return RestoreResult{}, err
319		}
320		if _, err := tx.Exec(
321			`INSERT INTO restores (document_id, change_id, device_id, snapshot_cursor, change_cursor, state)
322			 VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)`,
323			documentID, changeID, deviceID, snapshotCursor, nextCursor, state,
324		); err != nil {
325			return RestoreResult{}, err
326		}
327		return RestoreResult{
328			ID:           changeID,
329			Created:      true,
330			Cursor:       nextCursor,
331			RestoredFrom: snapshotCursor,
332		}, nil
333	}

1	// Document-level deletion removes every durable row a document owns in the
2	// change event service: the online change log, the compaction boundary, the
3	// retained idempotency summaries of trimmed changes, snapshots and restore
4	// provenance. After the deletion the same document id is a brand-new document:
5	// an unknown document reads as an empty list at cursor 0, and the next commit
6	// allocates cursor 1 again, because every row — the boundary included — that
7	// remembered the old cursor space is gone.
8	//
9	// The work runs inside the caller's serialized transaction, sharing it with the
10	// CRDT state and permission-ledger deletions of the same operation, so a
11	// document deletion either removes every row or none; a document with no row
12	// in any of the services misses (ErrDocumentNotFound) and writes nothing.
13	
14	package events
15	
16	import (
17		"errors"
18	
19		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/store"
20	)
21	
22	// ErrDocumentNotFound reports that a delete targets a document id that has no
23	// durable data anywhere — it was never created or was already deleted. The
24	// caller maps it to 404; nothing is written.
25	var ErrDocumentNotFound = errors.New("document not found")
26	
27	// DocumentDataExistsTx reports whether the change event service holds any row
28	// for documentID: an online change, a compaction boundary, a retained
29	// trimmed-id summary, a snapshot or a restore record. It runs inside the
30	// caller's transaction so the existence verdict is one judgment with the
31	// deletion that follows it.
32	func (s *Service) DocumentDataExistsTx(q store.DBTX, documentID string) (bool, error) {
33		var exists bool
34		if err := q.QueryRow(
35			`SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM changes WHERE document_id = ?)
36			 OR EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM change_boundaries WHERE document_id = ?)
37			 OR EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM change_identities WHERE document_id = ?)
38			 OR EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM snapshots WHERE document_id = ?)
39			 OR EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM restores WHERE document_id = ?)`,
40			documentID, documentID, documentID, documentID, documentID,
41		).Scan(&exists); err != nil {
42			return false, err
43		}
44		return exists, nil
45	}
46	
47	// DeleteDocumentDataTx removes every change-event row of documentID inside the
48	// caller's serialized transaction: the online log and restore records first
49	// (the rows that reference cursors), then snapshots, the retained idempotency
50	// summaries and finally the compaction boundary. With the boundary gone the
51	// cursor space restarts from 1 when the id is created again. It does not
52	// judge existence — the caller checks DocumentDataExistsTx (and the CRDT
53	// service's equivalent) once before deleting — so it never returns
54	// ErrDocumentNotFound on its own.
55	func (s *Service) DeleteDocumentDataTx(q store.DBTX, documentID string) error {
56		stmts := []string{
57			`DELETE FROM restores WHERE document_id = ?`,
58			`DELETE FROM changes WHERE document_id = ?`,
59			`DELETE FROM snapshots WHERE document_id = ?`,
60			`DELETE FROM change_identities WHERE document_id = ?`,
61			`DELETE FROM change_boundaries WHERE document_id = ?`,
62		}
63		for _, stmt := range stmts {
64			if _, err := q.Exec(stmt, documentID); err != nil {
65				return err
66			}
67		}
68		return nil
69	}
70

1	// Package authz is the permission service: the durable, per-document and
2	// per-device authorization ledger together with the system's single revoke
3	// verdict.
4	//
5	// Every (document, device) pair starts authorized; a grant or revoke is
6	// recorded per pair. The lookup and the write run in one serialized
7	// transaction on the shared connection and commit to disk, so concurrent
8	// grant/revoke calls each land as a complete state and survive a restart.
9	//
10	// The other services do not read the permission table. They take their
11	// registration-and-authorization verdict through AuthorizedTx, evaluated
12	// inside their own write transaction, so a rejected request is judged before
13	// any document content is observed and the gate and the gated work commit as
14	// one judgment. Revoking never deletes changes, snapshots, sessions or CRDT
15	// state; it only produces the denial and, after the revoke commits, notifies
16	// the registered revoke sinks (the live subscription registries) so they can
17	// end the affected connections with the one-time, sticky 4403 close.
18	package authz
19	
20	import (
21		"database/sql"
22		"errors"
23		"sync"
24	
25		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/store"
26	)
27	
28	// schema is created when the service is constructed; its shape is unchanged
29	// from the pre-refactor layout, so authorization rows already on disk stay
30	// readable.
31	const schema = `
32	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS document_permissions (
33		document_id TEXT NOT NULL,
34		device_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
35		authorized  INTEGER NOT NULL,
36		PRIMARY KEY (document_id, device_id)
37	);
38	`
39	
40	// RevokeSink observes a committed revoke. The change event service and the
41	// CRDT service register themselves to end the affected live subscriptions; a
42	// sink must not block and must be safe to call after the revoke transaction
43	// has committed. The permission service depends on this interface alone, so
44	// the dependency points from the observers toward the verdict and never back.
45	type RevokeSink interface {
46		PermissionRevoked(documentID, deviceID string)
47	}
48	
49	// Service is the permission service.
50	type Service struct {
51		db *sql.DB
52	
53		mu    sync.Mutex
54		sinks []RevokeSink
55	}
56	
57	// New constructs the permission service over the shared kernel handle and
58	// creates its table.
59	func New(kernel *store.Store) (*Service, error) {
60		db := kernel.DB()
61		if _, err := db.Exec(schema); err != nil {
62			return nil, err
63		}
64		return &Service{db: db}, nil
65	}
66	
67	// AddRevokeSink registers an observer notified after every committed revoke.
68	// It is called by the composition root while wiring the services, before the
69	// surface serves requests.
70	func (s *Service) AddRevokeSink(sink RevokeSink) {
71		s.mu.Lock()
72		s.sinks = append(s.sinks, sink)
73		s.mu.Unlock()
74	}
75	
76	// AuthorizedTx is the shared gate: it returns nil when deviceID is registered
77	// and currently authorized for documentID, store.ErrDeviceNotFound when the
78	// device is not registered and store.ErrPermissionDenied when its access has
79	// been revoked. It runs inside the caller's transaction q, so the verdict is
80	// taken on the same serialized connection as the work it guards, before any
81	// document content is read.
82	func (s *Service) AuthorizedTx(q store.DBTX, documentID, deviceID string) error {
83		exists, err := store.DeviceExistsTx(q, deviceID)
84		if err != nil {
85			return err
86		}
87		if !exists {
88			return store.ErrDeviceNotFound
89		}
90		var stored int
91		err = q.QueryRow(
92			`SELECT authorized FROM document_permissions WHERE document_id = ? AND device_id = ?`,
93			documentID, deviceID,
94		).Scan(&stored)
95		switch {
96		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
97			// No deviation row: devices start authorized.
98			return nil
99		case err != nil:
100			return err
101		default:
102			if stored == 0 {
103				return store.ErrPermissionDenied
104			}
105			return nil
106		}
107	}
108	
109	// DeviceAuthorizedTx adapts the shared gate to the change event and CRDT
110	// services' Gate interface (which names *sql.Tx). The verdict is identical.
111	func (s *Service) DeviceAuthorizedTx(tx *sql.Tx, documentID, deviceID string) error {
112		return s.AuthorizedTx(tx, documentID, deviceID)
113	}
114	
115	// SetDocumentPermission grants or revokes deviceID's access to documentID and
116	// reports whether the stored permission actually changed.
117	//
118	// Every device starts authorized for every document, so the first revoke is
119	// the first write for the pair (changed=true); repeating a state that already
120	// holds writes nothing and reports changed=false. An unregistered device
121	// yields store.ErrDeviceNotFound and nothing is written. The lookup and the
122	// write run in one serialized transaction, so concurrent grant/revoke calls
123	// each commit completely and the final state matches the last committed
124	// action. After a revoke commits, every registered sink is notified; a grant
125	// notifies nothing (a prior revoke already ended the connection stickily).
126	func (s *Service) SetDocumentPermission(documentID, deviceID string, authorized bool) (changed bool, err error) {
127		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
128		if err != nil {
129			return false, err
130		}
131		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
132	
133		exists, err := store.DeviceExistsTx(tx, deviceID)
134		if err != nil {
135			return false, err
136		}
137		if !exists {
138			return false, store.ErrDeviceNotFound
139		}
140	
141		current := true // devices start authorized; a row only records a deviation
142		var stored int
143		err = tx.QueryRow(
144			`SELECT authorized FROM document_permissions WHERE document_id = ? AND device_id = ?`,
145			documentID, deviceID,
146		).Scan(&stored)
147		switch {
148		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
149			// No row: the default (authorized) holds.
150		case err != nil:
151			return false, err
152		default:
153			current = stored != 0
154		}
155		if current == authorized {
156			return false, tx.Commit()
157		}
158	
159		v := 0
160		if authorized {
161			v = 1
162		}
163		if _, err := tx.Exec(
164			`INSERT INTO document_permissions (document_id, device_id, authorized) VALUES (?, ?, ?)
165			 ON CONFLICT (document_id, device_id) DO UPDATE SET authorized = excluded.authorized`,
166			documentID, deviceID, v,
167		); err != nil {
168			return false, err
169		}
170		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
171			return false, err
172		}
173	
174		// A grant cannot unblock a subscription (the first revoke already ended
175		// it, stickily); only a revoke needs to end live subscriptions.
176		if !authorized {
177			s.mu.Lock()
178			sinks := append([]RevokeSink(nil), s.sinks...)
179			s.mu.Unlock()
180			for _, sink := range sinks {
181				sink.PermissionRevoked(documentID, deviceID)
182			}
183		}
184		return true, nil
185	}
186	
187	// DeleteDevicePermissionsTx removes every document-permission ledger row that
188	// names deviceID, inside the caller's transaction: grants and revokes the
189	// deregistered device held on documents vanish together with the device. It is
190	// the permission service's share of device deregistration, run in the same
191	// serialized transaction as the registration layer's cascade, so the row
192	// removals and the device deletion commit as one judgment. After the device
193	// row is gone the default verdict would be "unregistered" anyway; clearing the
194	// rows guarantees a device that later re-registers the same id starts with no
195	// inherited authorization state.
196	func (s *Service) DeleteDevicePermissionsTx(q store.DBTX, deviceID string) error {
197		_, err := q.Exec(
198			`DELETE FROM document_permissions WHERE device_id = ?`, deviceID,
199		)
200		return err
201	}
202	
203	// DocumentHasRowsTx reports whether the ledger holds any row (a grant or a
204	// revoke deviation) for documentID. It is part of document existence: a
205	// document whose only durable trace is a permission deviation still exists and
206	// can be deleted so that the same id is later a brand-new document with no
207	// inherited authorization state.
208	func (s *Service) DocumentHasRowsTx(q store.DBTX, documentID string) (bool, error) {
209		var exists bool
210		if err := q.QueryRow(
211			`SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM document_permissions WHERE document_id = ?)`,
212			documentID,
213		).Scan(&exists); err != nil {
214			return false, err
215		}
216		return exists, nil
217	}
218	
219	// DeleteDocumentPermissionsTx removes every permission-ledger row that names
220	// documentID, inside the caller's transaction: the per-device grant/revoke
221	// deviations of a deleted document vanish with it, so when the same id is
222	// created again every pair starts from the default (authorized) with no
223	// inherited ledger state. It is the permission service's share of document
224	// deletion, run in the same serialized transaction as the change-event and
225	// CRDT cascades, so the row removals and the document deletion commit as one
226	// judgment.
227	func (s *Service) DeleteDocumentPermissionsTx(q store.DBTX, documentID string) error {
228		_, err := q.Exec(
229			`DELETE FROM document_permissions WHERE document_id = ?`, documentID,
230		)
231		return err
232	}
233	
234	// DocumentAuthorized reports whether deviceID currently holds permission for
235	// documentID. Devices start authorized, so an absent row means authorized.
236	func (s *Service) DocumentAuthorized(documentID, deviceID string) (bool, error) {
237		var stored int
238		err := s.db.QueryRow(
239			`SELECT authorized FROM document_permissions WHERE document_id = ? AND device_id = ?`,
240			documentID, deviceID,
241		).Scan(&stored)
242		switch {
243		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
244			return true, nil
245		case err != nil:
246			return false, err
247		default:
248			return stored != 0, nil
249		}
250	}
251	
252	// PermissionEntry is one row of a document's permission ledger: a currently
253	// registered device id together with its authorization for the document.
254	type PermissionEntry struct {
255		DeviceID   string
256		Authorized bool
257	}
258	
259	// ListDocumentPermissions is the read-only ledger view of one document: one
260	// entry per currently registered device, in ascending lexicographic device-id
261	// order, paged by limit/offset against that same order.
262	//
263	// A device with no ledger row starts authorized, so its entry reports
264	// Authorized=true; a device whose latest committed action was a revoke reports
265	// false. Deregistered devices carry no device row and their ledger rows were
266	// removed by the deregistration cascade, so they never appear. An unknown
267	// document is indistinguishable from one on which every device keeps the
268	// default: every registered device lists authorized. The read runs in one
269	// serialized transaction, creates no row, moves no cursor and notifies no sink.
270	func (s *Service) ListDocumentPermissions(documentID string, limit, offset int64) ([]PermissionEntry, error) {
271		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
272		if err != nil {
273			return nil, err
274		}
275		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
276	
277		rows, err := tx.Query(
278			`SELECT d.id, COALESCE(p.authorized, 1) AS authorized

3	import (
4		"context"
5		"database/sql"

9	// DocumentExists reports whether documentID is a known document rather than an
10	// empty namespace: it has any online change row, or a compaction boundary from
11	// a log that was (fully or partially) trimmed.
12	func (s *Service) DocumentExists(documentID string) (bool, error) {
13		var known bool
14		if err := s.db.QueryRow(
15			`SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM changes WHERE document_id = ?)
16			 OR EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM change_boundaries WHERE document_id = ?)`,
17			documentID, documentID,
18		).Scan(&known); err != nil {
19			return false, err
20		}
21		return known, nil
22	}
23	
24	// ListChanges returns at most limit changes for documentID whose cursor is
25	// greater than after and still online, in cursor order, together with the
26	// cursor to pass as the next after value. An unknown document yields an empty
27	// list and cursor 0; a known document with no rows past after yields
28	// nextCursor == max(after, boundary), so a caller positioned inside the
29	// trimmed range resumes from the compaction boundary.
30	func (s *Service) ListChanges(documentID string, after, limit int64) ([]ListedChange, int64, error) {
31		rows, err := s.db.Query(
32			`SELECT id, device_id, payload, cursor FROM changes
33			 WHERE document_id = ? AND cursor > ?
34			 ORDER BY cursor ASC
35			 LIMIT ?`,
36			documentID, after, limit,
37		)
38		if err != nil {
39			return nil, 0, err
40		}
41		defer func() { _ = rows.Close() }()
42	
43		out := make([]ListedChange, 0)
44		var maxCursor int64 = after
45		for rows.Next() {
46			var c ListedChange
47			if err := rows.Scan(&c.ID, &c.DeviceID, &c.Payload, &c.Cursor); err != nil {
48				return nil, 0, err
49			}
50			out = append(out, c)
51			maxCursor = c.Cursor
52		}
53		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
54			return nil, 0, err
55		}
56	
57		// Distinguish an unknown document from a known one with nothing new:
58		// unknown documents must report nextCursor 0, while a known document
59		// reports the greater of after and the compaction boundary.
60		if len(out) == 0 {
61			known, err := s.DocumentExists(documentID)
62			if err != nil {
63				return nil, 0, err
64			}
65			if !known {
66				return out, 0, nil
67			}
68			boundary, err := boundaryOfTx(s.db, documentID)
69			if err != nil {
70				return nil, 0, err
71			}
72			if boundary > maxCursor {
73				maxCursor = boundary
74			}
75		}
76		return out, maxCursor, nil
77	}
78	
79	// ExportChanges returns every change of documentID whose cursor lies in the
80	// closed interval [from, to] and is still in the online log, in ascending
81	// cursor order. When to is nil no upper bound is applied. An unknown document,
82	// or a range without any online change — including one that lies entirely
83	// inside the trimmed region — yields an empty list and no error: the export is
84	// a read that misses like any other. The (document_id, cursor) unique index
85	// guarantees a cursor appears at most once.
86	//
87	// The single SELECT runs as one SQLite statement over the serialized
88	// connection, so a batch committed concurrently is observed either with all of
89	// its rows or not at all — never half of it. The read starts no transaction,
90	// writes nothing and notifies no waiters, so it cannot move a cursor, produce
91	// a change record or wake a parked poll. Each returned row is the same record
92	// the paged read emits at that cursor.
93	func (s *Service) ExportChanges(documentID string, from int64, to *int64) ([]ListedChange, error) {
94		var (
95			rows *sql.Rows
96			err  error
97		)
98		if to == nil {
99			rows, err = s.db.Query(
100				`SELECT id, device_id, payload, cursor FROM changes
101				 WHERE document_id = ? AND cursor >= ?
102				 ORDER BY cursor ASC`,
103				documentID, from,
104			)
105		} else {
106			rows, err = s.db.Query(
107				`SELECT id, device_id, payload, cursor FROM changes
108				 WHERE document_id = ? AND cursor >= ? AND cursor <= ?
109				 ORDER BY cursor ASC`,
110				documentID, from, *to,
111			)
112		}
113		if err != nil {
114			return nil, err
115		}
116		defer func() { _ = rows.Close() }()
117	
118		out := make([]ListedChange, 0)
119		for rows.Next() {
120			var c ListedChange
121			if err := rows.Scan(&c.ID, &c.DeviceID, &c.Payload, &c.Cursor); err != nil {
122				return nil, err
123			}
124			out = append(out, c)
125		}
126		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
127			return nil, err
128		}
129		return out, nil
130	}
131	
132	// WaitForChanges blocks until documentID has a change with cursor greater than
133	// after, a change is committed while waiting, wait elapses, ctx is canceled
134	// (the client disconnected) or the service stops. It then returns the current
135	// page of up to limit changes exactly as ListChanges would, with timedOut=true
136	// only when the wait deadline expired with no new rows.
137	//
138	// Registration precedes the first query: a commit landing between the read and
139	// the park still notifies a registered channel, so no change is missed.
140	//
141	// An unknown document is never parked on: it returns immediately with an empty
142	// list and nextCursor 0, timedOut=false. Data already past after is likewise
143	// returned immediately. wait <= 0 is an immediately expired deadline.
144	func (s *Service) WaitForChanges(ctx context.Context, documentID string, after, limit int64, wait time.Duration) (changes []ListedChange, nextCursor int64, timedOut bool, err error) {
145		ch, remove := s.registerWait(documentID)
146		defer remove()
147	
148		changes, nextCursor, err = s.ListChanges(documentID, after, limit)
149		if err != nil || len(changes) > 0 {
150			return changes, nextCursor, false, err
151		}
152	
153		// Empty page: distinguish an unknown document (immediate empty/0, never
154		// parked on) from a known document caught up to after.
155		known, err := s.DocumentExists(documentID)
156		if err != nil || !known {
157			return changes, 0, false, err
158		}
159	
160		// Known document, nothing new: a zero wait is an immediately expired
161		// deadline; ListChanges already echoes nextCursor == after.
162		if wait <= 0 {
163			return changes, nextCursor, true, nil
164		}
165	
166		timer := time.NewTimer(wait)
167		defer timer.Stop()
168	
169		select {
170		case <-ch:
171			// Woken by a committed change, a whole-document deletion, or
172			// InterruptWaits. A deleted document is an unknown document now: answer
173			// an empty page at cursor 0 with timedOut=false rather than reporting a
174			// deadline expiry. Any other empty re-read keeps the old timeout shape.
175			s.mu.Lock()
176			closing := s.closed
177			s.mu.Unlock()
178			if closing {
179				return nil, 0, false, ErrStoreClosing
180			}
181			changes, nextCursor, err = s.ListChanges(documentID, after, limit)
182			if err != nil {
183				return nil, 0, false, err
184			}
185			if len(changes) == 0 {
186				known, knownErr := s.DocumentExists(documentID)
187				if knownErr != nil {
188					return nil, 0, false, knownErr
189				}
190				if !known {
191					return changes, 0, false, nil
192				}
193			}
194			return changes, nextCursor, len(changes) == 0, err
195		case <-timer.C:
196			// Timeout with no new rows: echo the caller's cursor without
197			// advancing it. The document was known above, so ListChanges returns
198			// nextCursor == after for an empty page.
199			changes, nextCursor, err = s.ListChanges(documentID, after, limit)
200			return changes, nextCursor, len(changes) == 0, err
201		case <-ctx.Done():
202			return nil, 0, false, ctx.Err()
203		}
204	}
205	
206	// registerWait parks a channel for documentID and returns it together with a
207	// removal function. The channel is closed on the next committed change to the
208	// document, or when the service stops.
209	func (s *Service) registerWait(documentID string) (ch chan struct{}, remove func()) {
210		ch = make(chan struct{}, 1)
211	
212		s.mu.Lock()
213		defer s.mu.Unlock()
214		if s.closed {
215			// Shutdown beat the registration: signal immediately so the caller does
216			// not park on a channel nobody will close.
217			close(ch)
218			return ch, func() {}
219		}
220		s.nextWait++
221		id := s.nextWait
222		set := s.waits[documentID]
223		if set == nil {
224			set = make(map[uint64]chan struct{})
225			s.waits[documentID] = set
226		}
227		set[id] = ch
228		return ch, func() {
229			s.mu.Lock()
230			if set, ok := s.waits[documentID]; ok {
231				delete(set, id)
232				if len(set) == 0 {
233					delete(s.waits, documentID)
234				}
235			}
236			s.mu.Unlock()
237		}
238	}
239	
240	// notifyWaiters signals every long poll parked on documentID and every
241	// subscription open on it. It is called only after a change-bearing
242	// transaction has committed, so parked readers observe the new rows when they
243	// re-query and pushed frames describe committed changes.
244	func (s *Service) notifyWaiters(documentID string) {
245		s.mu.Lock()
246		set := s.waits[documentID]
247		delete(s.waits, documentID)
248		s.mu.Unlock()
249		for _, ch := range set {
250			close(ch)
251		}
252		s.signalSubscribers(documentID)
253	}

1	package server

3	import (
